key_insight: Multi-agent systems help when bounded communication compresses redundant context more than it loses task-relevant information, making them an information-bottleneck trade-off rather than a universal upgrade over single-agent systems.
engineering_relevance: For LLM system design, the best architecture depends on relay bandwidth and model strength: near-sufficient communication can improve efficiency, but lossy message passing can reduce performance, especially for stronger models.
method: Formulate SAS vs. MAS as an information bottleneck with bounded relay messages.
Show that with infinite relay bandwidth, a MAS can simulate any SAS by transmitting full context.
Introduce an effective bottleneck parameter β to capture the compression–information-loss trade-off.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the theory with 18 controlled experiments across five benchmarks and three model scales, finding MAS gains when relays are near-sufficient and weaker models benefit most.
watch_item: The benefit of MAS is sensitive to communication design; if relay messages discard too much information, performance can stagnate or reverse despite added coordination overhead.
paper_title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
